title: Optimization of mito-roGFP protocol to measure mitochondrial oxidative status in human coronary artery endothelial cells
protocol: Plate 30,000 cells per 35 mm μ-Dish.
Coat each 35 mm μ-Dish with 1 mL of 0.1% gelatin and incubate for 30 min to 1 h in the incubator.
Remove excess gelatin from the plate.
Wash the cells with DPBS (10 mL).
Trypsinize the cells (2 mL/10 cm plate, incubate for 2 min, then visualize that cells have detached).
Inactivate trypsin (6 mL of TNS/10 cm plate).
Centrifuge (800 × g, 5 min).
Resuspend in 3 mL of growth media and estimate the cell density using a hemocytometer or an automated cell counter.
Remove excess gelatin from the μ-dishes.
Add 1 mL of growth media containing a volume of cell suspension equivalent to 30,000 cells.
Incubate cells in a cell culture incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2, and 85%-95% humidity for 16 hours.
Plate 1 mL of cell suspension with 9 mL of growth media into a 10 cm plate.
Replace the media with fresh media containing 5 μL of Mito-roGFP suspension per mL.
Add 1 mL of Mito-roGFP-containing media to each dish.
Incubate cells in a cell culture incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2, and 85%-95% humidity for 16 hours.
Change the media prior to starting the imaging procedure with fresh media.
Discard all tips and media containing Mito-roGFP in a waste container with 10% bleach solution.
Prepare 100 mM DTT stock solution as described in materials and equipment section.
Label 3 tubes per sample: pipette 515 μL of HBSS into one tube, pipette 100 μL of HBSS into another tube, and pipette 52.5 μL of HBSS into the third tube.
Keep HBSS tubes in a 37°C water bath until ready to use.
Turn on microscope and all its accessories (fluorescence light, camera) at least 20 minutes before imaging.
Open the imaging program.
Click on the live multichannel button.
Select 40× at the nosepiece window.
At the ND Acquisition panel, click “Load” and select “Load from XML file….”
Select the file named as “Mito-roGFP TEMPLATE.xml.”
Check all settings to confirm successful loading of the template.
Select the mito-roGFP (405 nm) channel.
Input data as shown in the yellow square of Figure 2A, step 5.
Select the FITC (488 nm) channel.
Input settings exactly as indicated in the yellow square for the FITC channel.
If setting up for HCAEC, change the exposure value to 1 s.
Set the exposure value to 200 milliseconds for Mito-roGFP and FITC channels.
Optimize exposure and gain for both 488 nm and 405 nm channels according to experimental conditions.
Confirm intervals and time for measurement (15 s interval, first loop 35 min, second loop 35 min).
Check boxes and edit all fields exactly as indicated in the yellow box in Figure 2B, step 3.
Click on the “Define ratio…” button.
Change the numerator to 405 nm and the denominator to 488 nm.
Check the box “keep color scale in view”.
Apply changes and close the ratio properties window.
At the ND Acquisition window, click on the subfield named as “Lambda”.
Confirm that only FITC and Mito-roGFP channels are selected.
Check the “close active shutter during filter change” box.
At the OC Panel window, check that the right filters are selected in the filter block for both 488 and 405 nm channels.
At the main window, click on “measure” and then on “Time measurement”.
Bring a control sample to the microscope.
Replace the media with 500 μL HBSS from tube 1.
Put 2-3 cells into focus.
Check FITC and mito-roGFP channels.
Adjust exposure and gain if necessary.
Click on “measure” at the main window.
Select “Simple ROI (Region Of Interest) Editor.”
Choose the “Bezier” tool to draw each ROI.
Select a region with no cells for background ROI.
Use right click button function of mousepad on top of ROI, select “use as background ROI.”
Draw around 20 test ROIs near the nuclei using Bezier tool.
Click the “finish” button in the toolbox.
Click the “ROIs” button in the ND Acquisition window.
Select and highlight ROIs for measurement.
Ensure all selected ROIs appear on the left side of the screen.
Verify that the ND Acquisition window shows the correct number of selected ROIs.
Organize all open windows to ensure clear visibility without overlapping.
At the time measurement window, select “Graph display” as “No split”.
Select “<min – max>” for graph display settings.
Click on the “Run now” button in the ND Acquisition window.
Select: “Left” as “ratio 405/488”.
Check if the ratio of all ROIs is, on average, close to 1.
Adjust exposure and gain of FITC and Mito-roGFP channels as needed.
Repeat step 6 (i-j) after adjusting settings.
Record cells for a minimum of three minutes before proceeding.
Prepare to pipette DTT solution.
Add 400 μL of DTT stock solution to the tube named as "2".
Wait 3 minutes after baseline recording begins.
Transfer all volume (500 μL) from the tube to the sample during the filter change interval (15 seconds).
Spread the DTT into the plate slowly without touching the plate.
Observe that ratiometric values should decrease and cells will appear in purple color.
Pause to watch the cells for 15 minutes, annotating any displaced ROIs.
Prepare to pipette H2O2 solution.
Add 47.5 μL of 3% H2O2 to the tube named as “3”.
Transfer all volume (100 μL) from the tube to the sample after fifteen minutes, without touching the plate.
Continue recording until the cells consistently present with red color.
Stop recording after seeing predominance of the red color throughout the entire cell for at least 5 frames.
Save and export all data in an ND2 format, properly identifying your sample.
Export an experimental report to excel, properly identifying your sample.
Close the main window used for acquisition.
Proceed to the next sample.
Focus the cells under the microscope.
Start from step 6, substep g of this protocol.
